Glossary

# dharma धर्म

the order that sustains things; also one's own duty; also a teaching

Sanskrit / Pali · glossed in English

[Glossary](https://www.philosophydef.com/glossary) / dharma

A term is not a word. It is a working part of somebody's argument, and the English word usually offered for it is a compromise. This page gives the compromise, the argument, and the reading the sources do not support.

Where it is filed: [Morality](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/morality) · [Responsibility](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/responsibility) · [Order](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/order) · [Truth](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/truth) · [Practice](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/practice) · [Action](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/action)

## What the term does

Dharma carries three senses that connect: the cosmic order that sustains the world, the specific duty that follows from one's position in that order, and — in Buddhism, where the Pali form is dhamma — the teaching and the constituent factors of experience. In the Gītā the second sense does the work: Arjuna's duty follows from his role, and Kṛṣṇa's argument depends on that duty being tied to a station rather than to a consequence. The Buddhist use is not a duty at all but an analysis of what a person is made of.

## The reading the sources do not support

In English, the word slides almost entirely into the third sense, as in 'the dharma' meaning a teaching, or into a vague sense of cosmic justice. Reading the Gītā through either of those makes its central argument about station and obligation hard to see.
